payload.message:
Decide attendance intervals for meetings on a shared timeline.

NOTE: If environment.assignment_filling=true and an agent fails to assign a variable, the environment will fill any remaining unassigned variables with a uniform-random allowed assignment when producing final results.

This blackboard is a private communication channel.
Participants: Avery, Jordan, Quinn, Reese, Riley, Taylor

payload.content: Reese planning note: I will likely fully attend strict meetings m001 [1,2), m008 [9,10), m016 [10,11), m010 [11,12). For soft meetings, to avoid self-overlap penalties I currently lean toward a non-overlapping chain such as early gaming/art before 1, one activity in 2-5, one in 5-9, then strict block 9-12, then volleyball after 12. Others, if useful, please share likely intervals for m002/m003/m006/m012/m015/m013/m009/m011/m005 so I can align overlaps without conflicts.

Riley planning: I will fully attend strict meetings m008 [9,10) and m016 [10,11). To avoid overlap penalties, my current soft plan is: choose m003 Gaming [0,3) for early block and skip/limit m002; choose m006 Board game [2,5) OR m015 Gaming [4,7) but not both overlapping; likely m009 Friends’ hangout [7,9) then m008, then m016, then m005 Volleyball [11,14). I probably will skip m011 [8,10) because it conflicts with strict m008, and skip m007 [10,13) because it conflicts with m016 and m005. If others want a different coordination anchor, please reply with likely intervals, especially for m003 vs m002 early, m006 vs m012 in [2,4), and whether m009 should end by 9 for m008.

Quinn planning draft: I expect to fully attend all my strict meetings m001 [1,2), m008 [9,10), m016 [10,11), m010 [11,12). To avoid self-overlap, my soft preference is a non-overlapping chain around them: early m003 Gaming [0,1) before class (rather than long m002), then one 2-4 activity—leaning m012 Music [2,4) and skip m006/m014/m004, then m015 Gaming [4,7), then m009 Friends [7,9) before m008, skip m011 due to conflict with m008, and after strict block choose m005 Volleyball [12,14), skipping m007. This would give anchors: m003 [0,1), m012 [2,4), m015 [4,7), m009 [7,9), m005 [12,14). If others can align to these intervals, good overlap without penalties. Especially interested whether Taylor/Jordan/Avery/Reese can also do m012 over m006 in [2,4), and whether m015/m009/m005 seem good common anchors.

Jordan planning draft: I expect to fully attend my strict meetings m001 [1,2), m008 [9,10), m016 [10,11), m010 [11,12). To avoid self-overlap penalties, my tentative soft chain is m002 Collaborative art [0,1) before class, then one 2-4 activity—leaning m012 Music [2,4) (and skipping m006/m014/m004), then m015 Gaming [4,7), then m009 Friends [7,9) before m008, skip m011 due to conflict with m008, and likely skip m007 because it overlaps m016 and m010. This is close to Quinn’s anchors except I’m slightly leaning m002 [0,1) instead of m003 since that’s one of my meetings. Happy to switch early anchor if broader coordination prefers art vs gaming; strongest preference is common anchors at m012 [2,4), m015 [4,7), m009 [7,9), plus full strict block [9,12). (phase=planning, iter=1)

Taylor planning draft: for strict meetings I plan full attendance m001 [1,2), m008 [9,10), m016 [10,11). To avoid self-overlap penalties, my tentative soft chain is early m003 Gaming [0,1) (rather than long m002), then one 2-4 activity—leaning m012 Music [2,4) and skipping m006/m014 plus likely m004, then m015 Gaming [4,7), and after the strict block m005 Volleyball [11,14). I likely skip m007 because it conflicts with m016 and m005. This aligns well with Quinn/Jordan on m012 and m015; Riley/Reese, if you can also use m003 [0,1), m012 [2,4), m015 [4,7), and m005 [11,14) or [12,14), we can create common overlap anchors without penalties. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Avery planning draft: to avoid self-overlap penalties, I currently lean toward the common-anchor chain m003 Gaming [0,1), m012 Music [2,4), m015 Gaming [4,7), m009 Friends [7,9) or possibly [7,10) since I do not have m008, then full strict m016 [10,11) and m010 [11,12). I lean skip m002, m006, m014, m013, and m011 because they overlap these anchors. Since several of you have m008 [9,10), I’m happy to use m009 [7,9) to preserve a clean handoff into stricts if that helps coordination. If anyone strongly prefers a different Avery-overlap target among m002 vs m003 early or m013 vs m015 later, let me know.

Reese updated planning: I can align with the emerging common-anchor chain with no self-overlap: m003 Gaming [0,1), full strict m001 [1,2), m012 Music [2,4), m015 Gaming [4,7), m009 Friends [7,9), full stricts m008 [9,10), m016 [10,11), m010 [11,12), and m005 Volleyball [12,14). I would then skip m002/m006/m004/m011/m013 to avoid conflicts. This seems to match Quinn/Taylor/Avery and mostly Jordan, and preserves overlap without penalties. If anyone sees a better adjustment, let me know, but this is my current likely commitment.

Riley updated planning: I can align with the emerging common-anchor chain and avoid self-overlap. Current likely commitments are m003 Gaming [0,1), m012 Music [2,4), m015 Gaming [4,7), m009 Friends [7,9), full strict m008 [9,10), full strict m016 [10,11), and m005 Volleyball [11,14). I would skip m002/m006/m011/m007 to avoid conflicts. This matches Quinn/Taylor/Reese/Avery on most anchors, and Jordan except for the early slot. Unless someone sees a better alternative, this is my likely execution plan. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Quinn update: strong consensus now appears to be the clean non-overlapping chain for shared reward: m003 [0,1), m001 [1,2), m012 [2,4), m015 [4,7), m009 [7,9), m008 [9,10), m016 [10,11), m010 [11,12) where applicable, and m005 [12,14) or [11,14) depending on participants. I plan to keep that exact Quinn schedule: m003 [0,1), m001 full, m012 [2,4), m015 [4,7), m009 [7,9), m008 full, m016 full, m010 full, m005 [12,14); skip m002/m006/m014/m004/m011/m007/m013. Jordan, if you are willing to switch early from m002 to m003 [0,1), that would complete the common early anchor too.

Jordan update: I’m happy to align fully with the emerging consensus chain. Current likely plan is m001 [1,2), m012 [2,4), m015 [4,7), m009 [7,9), m008 [9,10), m016 [10,11), m010 [11,12), and skip m002/m006/m014/m004/m011/m007/m013. For the early slot, since m003 is not one of my meetings, my clean Jordan-specific equivalent is to skip m002 rather than create overlap elsewhere. So I won’t provide an early anchor at [0,1), but I can match the rest of the chain exactly with no self-overlap penalties. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Taylor update: I’m aligned with the apparent consensus chain and expect to execute exactly this for my meetings: m003 [0,1), m001 [1,2), m012 [2,4), m015 [4,7), m008 [9,10), m016 [10,11), m005 [11,14); skip m002, m006, m014, m004, m007. This avoids all self-overlap and matches Riley/Reese/Quinn/Avery on the main soft anchors, with Jordan joining from [1,2) onward. Unless anyone flags a better adjustment, I’ll keep this for execution.

Reese final planning signal: I’m settled on the consensus no-overlap chain for execution unless conditions change: m003 [0,1), m001 [1,2), m012 [2,4), m015 [4,7), m009 [7,9), m008 [9,10), m016 [10,11), m010 [11,12), m005 [12,14). I’ll skip m002/m006/m004/m011/m013. This should preserve broad overlap and zero self-conflict.

Riley final planning signal: I’m settled on the consensus no-overlap chain for execution unless conditions change: m003 [0,1), m012 [2,4), m015 [4,7), m009 [7,9), m008 [9,10) full, m016 [10,11) full, and m005 [11,14). I’ll skip m002/m006/m011/m007 to avoid self-overlap. This matches the shared anchors and should give strong overlap rewards with no self-conflict. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Quinn final planning confirmation: I’m locked on the consensus no-overlap chain for execution—m003 [0,1), m001 [1,2), m012 [2,4), m015 [4,7), m009 [7,9), m008 [9,10), m016 [10,11), m010 [11,12), m005 [12,14); skip m002/m006/m014/m004/m011/m007/m013. This matches the broad group anchors and should maximize overlap rewards while avoiding all self-overlap penalties. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Jordan final planning confirmation: I’m locked on the Jordan no-overlap chain for execution—m001 [1,2), m012 [2,4), m015 [4,7), m009 [7,9), m008 [9,10), m016 [10,11), m010 [11,12); skip m002/m006/m014/m004/m011/m007/m013. I’ll also skip the early [0,1) slot since m003 is not one of my meetings. This matches the shared anchors from class onward and avoids all self-overlap penalties. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Taylor final planning confirmation: no change from my draft. I’m locked on m003 [0,1), m001 [1,2), m012 [2,4), m015 [4,7), m008 [9,10), m016 [10,11), m005 [11,14); skip m002, m006, m014, m004, m007. This keeps zero self-overlap and matches the consensus anchors with Riley/Reese/Quinn/Avery, with Jordan aligned from [1,2) onward. Ready to execute this if phase changes. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Avery final planning confirmation: I’m locked on the consensus no-overlap chain for execution on my meetings—m003 [0,1), m012 [2,4), m015 [4,7), m009 [7,9), m016 [10,11), m010 [11,12); skip m002, m006, m014, m013, m011, m007. This avoids all self-overlap and matches Reese/Quinn/Riley/Taylor plus Jordan from [2,4) onward. Ready to execute if phase changes. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Riley planning confirmation: no change. I’m locked on m003 [0,1), m012 [2,4), m015 [4,7), m009 [7,9), full strict m008 [9,10), full strict m016 [10,11), and m005 [11,14); skip m002/m006/m011/m007. This preserves zero self-overlap and matches the consensus anchors. Ready to execute when phase changes. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Jordan planning status: no change from my final draft. I’m locked on m001 [1,2), m012 [2,4), m015 [4,7), m009 [7,9), m008 [9,10), m016 [10,11), m010 [11,12); skip m002/m006/m014/m004/m011/m007/m013. This keeps zero self-overlap and aligns with the consensus chain from class onward. Ready to execute when phase changes. (phase=planning, iter=1)

What intervals are you leaning toward?

Avery coalition reply: I can align with you on a no-self-overlap chain. My current best draft is m003 [0,1), m012 [2,4), m015 [4,7), m009 [7,10) or [7,9), then strict m016 [10,11) and m010 [11,12). Since I do not have m008, m009 [7,10) is feasible for me, but if broader group coordination wants everyone to avoid overlap with their m008 at 9, I can instead do m009 [7,9). I also have m011 [8,10), but that overlaps m009 and stricts, so I lean skip m011. m013 [5,8) conflicts with m015 [4,7), so I prefer m015 over m013 unless coalition specifically wants m013. Early m002 [0,4) also conflicts with m003/m012, so I lean skip m002. Main coalition-preferred anchors from my side: m003 [0,1), m012 [2,4), m015 [4,7), m009 [7,9] or [7,10), full m016, full m010.

Coalition update from Reese: your chain m003 [0,1), m012 [2,4), m015 [4,7), m009 [7,9), m016 [10,11), m010 [11,12) matches my current best response too. This gives us coalition overlap on m003/m012/m015/m009 plus strict m016/m010. Unless you see a better coalition gain, I’ll advocate this chain publicly too.

Coalition confirmation from Avery: I agree our best coalition plan is the clean chain m003 [0,1), m012 [2,4), m015 [4,7), m009 [7,9), then full strict m016 [10,11) and m010 [11,12). I will likely skip m002/m006/m014/m013/m011/m007 to avoid self-overlap. This maximizes our Avery-Reese overlaps on m003/m012/m015/m009 plus strict overlap on m016 and m010.
